body:
Stonepeak got a taste of Australian-listed funds last year, when it raised $300 million through a debt note. Now, the New York-based infrastructure investor is back for a second bite of the cherry.

Stonepeak’s broker syndicate – E&P Capital, National Australia Bank, Morgans Corporate and FIIG Securities – is testing the waters for a listed trust with a six-year term that would invest in infrastructure debt with the goal of delivering between 3.5 per cent and 4 per cent above the swaps.

Sarah Thompson has co-edited Street Talk since 2009, specialising in private equity, investment banking, M&A and equity capital markets stories. Prior to that, she spent 10 years in London as a markets and M&A reporter at Bloomberg and Dow Jones.

Kanika Sood is a journalist based in Sydney who writes for the Street Talk column.

Angira Bharadwaj is a co-editor of Street Talk. She covers IPOs, capital raises, mergers and acquisitions and other breaking news in Australia’s capital markets.
